newsitem.title: UK: LME copper takes rest, lead spirals lower.
newsitem.headline: LME copper takes rest, lead spirals lower.

text.p: LME copper took a breath on Tuesday afternoon, looking for a comfortable lower level, while lead slumped to a fresh 18-month nadir and was vulnerable to more losses, traders said.
All of the other metals ended the day softer except aluminium, which kept up a robust performance.

Three months copper ended the afternoon kerb little changed after testing both sides of the market, drifting to $2,346 per tonne in the morning and climbing to $2,374 after lunch. Last business was $4 up at $2,360.
The spreads also sought to stabilise after Monday's battering, with the benchmark cash/threes settling slightly narrower at a $65/$75 backwardation.
After Tuesday's fresh deliveries into LME warehouses, limiting the stocks fall to only 725 tonnes, the market would be watching closely inventory levels for the future direction of the spreads.
"The backwardation has done its work...potentially we could now see some stock rises," said analyst Robin Bahr of broker Brandeis.
There was still potential for spreads flaring, since tight prompts were seen extending to the May date, traders said.
"But it's going to take quite a bit to push it back to $200," said Bahr, referring to the peak backwardation of the cash/threes hit on Monday and Friday.
Lead spiralled lower after breaching the bottom of its recent range, ending $15 lower at $615, the lowest level since October 12, 1995.
"The charts are looking very weak...below where we are now there isn't a lot of support," said Bahr.
Support was pegged at $610/15, $600, and $580.

The main winter battery replacement season was well behind the market, while more supply was likely to be seen as Metaleurop's Nordenham plant and Cominco's Trail plant in Canada gear up for full production, he added.
Aluminium shook off the weakness in the others and continued to forge higher, ending the day $9 firmer at $1,637.50.
Players were looking for higher numbers eventually, but believe that the market may need to consolidate its recent gains before attacking resistance at $1,642, $1,650 and $1,680.
Zinc ended barely changed, down $3 at $1,264, after trading between $1,272 and $1,261. The market will be eyeing stocks data for signs of Chinese material heading for Singapore.
Nickel fared less well, ending the day well below the 10-day moving average at $7,280 with a $180 loss.
Any further falls should find good support at $7,110, which put a floor on the downside on April 14 and January 29.
Tin was also looking shaky, ending the kerb $65 weaker at its low of $5,650, down $65.
The market was in danger of retesting its April 11 low of $5,600, analysts said.
Alloy ended little changed at $1,505.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
